The park covers three volcanic cones: Mount Taranaki and its slopes, Pouākai and Kaitake. The park was first created in 1881 as a forest reserve and went on to become New Zealand’s second national park, preceded by Tongariro National Park, in 1900.
The forest reserve was created within a six-mile (9.7 km) radius around the cone of the dormant Mount Taranaki volcano. Areas encompassing the older volcanic remnants of Pouākai and Kaitake were later added to the reserve at the northwest side. The forest is surrounded on all sides by pasture, giving it a distinctly circular shape.
The official name of the park was changed from Egmont National Park to Te Papa-Kura-o-Taranaki on 1 April 2025.


== History ==


=== Early Māori history and legends ===
Mount Taranaki (Mt Egmont) is considered sacred by local Māori people who believe the mountain is where their ancestors descended from. Māori legend talks of Taranaki being called Pukeonaki and initially resided in central New Zealand next to Ruapehu, Tongariro, and Pihanga.
